second attempt at Jupiter with a 90mm Mak-Cass and a DSLR

This is another photo I took a few months ago, but I thought I'd submit it here to try to help as we try to get this subverse going.

This was shot 2015-03-30 at about 10:00 PM Mountain Daylight Time from my front yard in rural southeast Idaho. Temperature was around 60 °F, seeing was pretty good.

This was shot through my Celestron C90 (90mm aperture, 1250 mm focal length, f/13.89 focal ratio) with a Nikon D7000 at prime focus and a 2x barlow. I shot about 200 frames (1/8", ISO 400) and stacked the best 50 or so. I processed the frames using PIPP for centering and cropping, AviStack for alignment, stacking, and wavelet sharpening, and Gimp for levels adjustment.

I think I've improved noticeably since my first attempt at Jupiter several months prior with the same equipment. Last time I was shooting using the DSLR's video mode, which gave me more frames but a lower resolution. This time I shot a lot fewer frames but they were a lot larger, so I think it allowed me to get more detail. I'm still not totally happy with the amount of noise and clarity, but I've learned a lot and I think I'm getting better.

I'm open to thoughts and suggestions!

I don't even worry about the ratios, honestly. I just throw the scraps in there and follow them with a couple handfuls of grass. It's also okay if you get bugs in there. Their poop makes it even more fertile, and if they get crushed or die in the compost then their bodies make it even more fertile as well. Honestly just make sure it has enough moisture, and try not to give it too much water. If you do add too much of anything to the compost, it's bad, but it will always recover. As for not having heat, just try adding more grass, and material in general to the compost.

I thought I had read bugs meant it wasn't hot enough and not hot enough meant it wasn't breaking down at all. I have had a few people now tell me bugs are good so did I just completely misunderstand the concept or is the 'bugs are bad' idea simply bunk to be ignored?

No matter what you do you will always have bugs in your compost, don't take them as a sign of anything. What you need to be looking for is feeling heat by exposing an inner part of the compost heap and putting the back of your hand near it without touching it. As long as you feel heat you're doing good. It might take a bit, but around a month's time to definitely 2 months time the compost heap should turn into dark brown/black. Once you get to that stage then you can apply it to the garden soil.

if it isn't already, you should keep the tumbler in full sun. no way it won't get hot enough. also, add the manure. i dont really ever worry about ratios...just try to put as much different junk in there as i can. for me it's mostly: mushrooms, veggie scraps, egg shells, leaves, chicken manure, wheat straw. when it's in there and looks like its getting wet/weird or smells bad i just throw it in a big compost pile i have. i sorta think the tumbler can get tooo hot, so i use it to start the decay and then dump it
